subject: Biotechnology
title: Stem Cell Technology
description: A quick win: understand Stem Cell Technology.

hook.text: A single stem cell can become a heart cell, a neuron, or a blood cell — unlimited potential in one package.

buildup.text: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent — they can differentiate into any of the body's 200+ cell types.

discovery.text: Yamanaka reprogrammed adult skin cells back to stem cells in 2006 — induced pluripotent stem cells, or iPSCs.

twist.text: iPSCs bypass the ethical debate over embryos — any adult cell can become a stem cell with four genes.

climax.text: Stem cells now grow mini-organs in labs — organoids that test drugs without animal experiments.

punchline.text: Any cell can become any cell — Yamanaka rewrote biology's rules.

quiz.question: What are induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)?
options: Stem cells harvested from embryos for research
Adult cells reprogrammed back to a stem cell state using specific genes
Cells that can only develop into blood cells
